# Index Tuning Report - G11 (Phase 2)

**Database:** `CampusSpaceManagement` (SQL Server, Developer edition)
**Dataset:** generated by `outputs/14-data-generator-G11/generate_data.py`
(3,015 users · 608 spaces · 100,024 bookings · 8,007 maintenance records ·
77,988 approvals · 40,199 usage sessions · 22,208 advisory acknowledgements ·
2,000 incident reports · 1,367 report consolidations · 2,657 space_facility
rows — **258,073 rows total**, zero overlapping approved bookings verified by
`validation.sql`).

**Method:** each query was executed with `SET STATISTICS IO ON` and
`SET STATISTICS TIME ON` after `DBCC DROPCLEANBUFFERS`, first with only the
Phase 1 default indexes (PK/FK/UNIQUE), then after creating the tuned
nonclustered indexes from `outputs/10-schema-migration-G11.sql`. Estimated
subtree cost was read from `SET SHOWPLAN_ALL` output (statement root node).

**SARGability check (before indexing):** all four queries already used the
explicit inequality overlap form `start_time < @x AND end_time > @y` (no
function wrapping the indexed columns), so no query refactoring was needed —
index creation alone produced the gains below.

---

## Query 1 — Booking Conflict Check

### 1. Query Description & Business Context
The guarded overlap scan embedded in `sp_AutoApproveBookingRequest` and
`sp_book_space_staff_approve` (`outputs/12-concurrency-implementation-G11.sql`).
It is the **serialization point** of the concurrency strategy: it runs on every
booking creation and approval, so it must be both correct and fast.

### 2. Target SQL
```sql
IF EXISTS (
    SELECT 1
    FROM dbo.bookings WITH (UPDLOCK, HOLDLOCK)
    WHERE space_id = @space_id
      AND status IN ('Approved', 'Checked In', 'Completed')
      AND start_time < @end_time
      AND end_time   > @start_time
)
```
Benchmarked for space 3745 (`GEN-00465`, the busiest generated space),
window 2026-03-01 12:00..12:45.

### 3. Baseline Performance (Before Indexing)
- Plan: **Clustered Index Scan** over all 100,024 booking rows with a residual
  `WHERE` predicate.
- Logical Reads: **1,185** · Physical Reads: 0
- CPU: **32 ms** · Elapsed: **47 ms**
- Estimated Subtree Cost: **1.22621**

### 4. Index Design & Justification
```sql
CREATE INDEX IX_bookings_space_time
    ON dbo.bookings (space_id, start_time, end_time)
    INCLUDE (status);
```
- **Equality first:** `space_id = @space_id` narrows to one space.
- **Range next:** `start_time < @end_time` becomes a seek predicate on the index
  key (the `end_time > @start_time` part is applied as a residual filter).
- **INCLUDE (status):** makes the index covering for the `status IN (...)` filter
  and eliminates key lookups.
- **Side benefit:** this same index supplies the key-range lock the pessimistic
  concurrency design relies on (UPDLOCK/HOLDLOCK serializes competing inserts).

### 5. Optimized Performance (After Indexing)
- Plan: **Index Seek** on `IX_bookings_space_time` (residual filters only).
- Logical Reads: **4** · Physical Reads: 0
- CPU: **0 ms** · Elapsed: **0 ms**
- Estimated Subtree Cost: **0.0035633**

### 6. Comparative Analysis
| Metric | Before Indexing | After Indexing | Improvement (%) |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Logical Reads | 1,185 | 4 | 99.7% |
| CPU Time (ms) | 32 | 0 | 100.0% |
| Elapsed Time (ms) | 47 | 0 | 100.0% |
| Subtree Cost | 1.22621 | 0.0035633 | 99.7% |
| Operator | Clustered Index Scan | Index Seek | — |

### 7. DML Overhead
Insert/delete on `bookings` now maintains one extra index (3 key columns +
status, ≈ 5 MB measured on the generated data). Given the booking rate (semester
peak), the write cost is negligible compared to the correctness-critical read
path, and the index is **mandatory** for the locking strategy — without it the
serialization point would scan the whole table under a range lock.

## Query 2 — Room Finder

### 1. Query Description & Business Context
Report Q3 from `outputs/16-analytical-queries-G11.sql` (RC-09): find available
spaces meeting a capacity, facility-list, and time-window constraint. Run
interactively by requesters while searching for a room.

### 2. Target SQL
```sql
SELECT DISTINCT s.space_id, s.space_code, s.space_name, s.space_type,
       s.building, s.floor, s.room_number, s.capacity, s.current_status
FROM dbo.spaces AS s
WHERE s.capacity >= @MinCapacity
  AND s.current_status NOT IN ('Temporarily Closed', 'Retired')
  AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM dbo.bookings AS b
                  WHERE b.space_id = s.space_id
                    AND b.status IN ('Approved','Checked In','Completed')
                    AND b.start_time < @ReqEnd AND b.end_time > @ReqStart)
  AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM dbo.maintenance_records AS m
                  WHERE m.space_id = s.space_id
                    AND m.impact_level = 'out-of-service'
                    AND (m.completion_time IS NULL OR m.completion_time > @ReqStart)
                    AND m.start_time < @ReqEnd)
  AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM @RequiredFacilities AS rf
                  WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM dbo.space_facility AS sf
                                    WHERE sf.space_id = s.space_id
                                      AND sf.catalog_id = rf.catalog_id));
```
Benchmarked for `@MinCapacity = 20`, facilities {1, 5} (Projector,
Air Conditioning), window 2026-03-02 09:00..12:00 (returns 3 qualifying
spaces). Note the status filter uses the Phase 2 domain
(`'Under Maintenance'` no longer exists — C2; out-of-service blocking is done
by the maintenance probe below).

### 3. Baseline Performance (Before Indexing)
- Plan: nested **Clustered Index Scans** — the per-space booking overlap probe
  re-scans the whole 100,024-row `bookings` table (one full scan shared across
  the anti-semi-join), and the maintenance probe scans all 8,007 maintenance
  rows.
- Logical Reads: **406,697** (bookings 378,917 + maintenance 27,400 +
  space_facility 201 + temp 162 + spaces 17) · Physical Reads: 0
- CPU: **4,562 ms** · Elapsed: **4,660 ms**
- Estimated Subtree Cost: **1.00609**

### 4. Index Design & Justification
```sql
CREATE INDEX IX_bookings_space_time
    ON dbo.bookings (space_id, start_time, end_time) INCLUDE (status);

CREATE INDEX IX_maintenance_records_space_time
    ON dbo.maintenance_records (space_id, start_time, completion_time)
    INCLUDE (impact_level, status);

CREATE INDEX IX_spaces_capacity_status
    ON dbo.spaces (capacity) INCLUDE (current_status, space_type, space_name);
```
- `IX_bookings_space_time`: turns the per-space overlap probe into an Index Seek
  (equality `space_id`, range `start_time < @ReqEnd`, residual `end_time`).
- `IX_maintenance_records_space_time`: same for the out-of-service probe —
  equality `space_id`, `impact_level` filter, range on start/completion.
- `IX_spaces_capacity_status`: satisfies the `capacity >= @MinCapacity` filter
  as a seek, covering `current_status` so the status filter needs no lookup.

### 5. Optimized Performance (After Indexing)
- Plan: **Index Seeks** for the booking and maintenance anti-semi-join probes
  (345 seeks / 288 seeks over the 608 candidate spaces).
- Logical Reads: **2,410** (bookings 1,442 + maintenance 588 +
  space_facility 201 + temp 162 + spaces 17) · Physical Reads: 0
- CPU: **63 ms** · Elapsed: **52 ms**
- Estimated Subtree Cost: **0.0757961**

### 6. Comparative Analysis
| Metric | Before Indexing | After Indexing | Improvement (%) |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Logical Reads | 406,697 | 2,410 | 99.4% |
| CPU Time (ms) | 4,562 | 63 | 98.6% |
| Elapsed Time (ms) | 4,660 | 52 | 98.9% |
| Subtree Cost | 1.00609 | 0.0757961 | 92.5% |
| Operator | Table/Index Scans | Index Seeks | — |

### 7. DML Overhead
Adds maintenance cost to inserts/deletes on `bookings`, `maintenance_records`
(already paid for by Query 1/3 indexes) and one small covering index on `spaces`
(≈ 0.20 MB measured). `spaces` DML is rare (setup-time data), so the index is
effectively free.

## Query 3 — Analytical Report: Approved Booking Hours per Space

### 1. Query Description & Business Context
Report Q1 from `outputs/16-analytical-queries-G11.sql` (RC-07): total approved
booking hours per space for a semester. Executed by the Facility Manager at the
end of each semester (low frequency, large scan).

### 2. Target SQL
```sql
SELECT s.space_id, s.space_code, s.space_name,
       COUNT(b.booking_id) AS approved_booking_count,
       ISNULL(SUM(DATEDIFF(MINUTE, b.start_time, b.end_time)) / 60.0, 0)
           AS total_approved_hours
FROM dbo.spaces AS s
LEFT JOIN dbo.bookings AS b
       ON b.space_id = s.space_id
      AND b.status IN ('Approved', 'Checked In', 'Completed')
      AND b.start_time >= @SemStart
      AND b.start_time <  @SemEnd
GROUP BY s.space_id, s.space_code, s.space_name
ORDER BY total_approved_hours DESC, s.space_code;
```
Benchmarked for the seed semester 2026-01-05 08:00 .. 2026-04-30 18:00.

### 3. Baseline Performance (Before Indexing)
- Plan: **Clustered Index Scan** of `bookings` (1,215 pages, 100,024 rows)
  feeding a Hash Aggregate, joined to `spaces`.
- Logical Reads: **1,232** (bookings 1,215 + spaces 17) · Physical Reads: 0
- CPU: **94 ms** · Elapsed: **107 ms**
- Estimated Subtree Cost: **1.49935**

### 4. Index Design & Justification
```sql
CREATE INDEX IX_bookings_status_time
    ON dbo.bookings (status, start_time, end_time) INCLUDE (space_id);
```
- **Equality first:** `status IN ('Approved','Checked In','Completed')` becomes
  three seek predicates on the leading key.
- **Range next:** `start_time >= @SemStart AND start_time < @SemEnd` bounds the
  semester window on the index key.
- **INCLUDE (space_id):** covers the join key, eliminating lookups during the
  aggregate.

### 5. Optimized Performance (After Indexing)
- Plan: **Index Seek on `IX_bookings_status_time`** (status + semester range,
  430 pages) + Hash Aggregate; the `spaces` clustered scan is unchanged
  (17 pages, 608 rows).
- Logical Reads: **447** (bookings 430 + spaces 17) · Physical Reads: 0
- CPU: **78 ms** · Elapsed: **84 ms**
- Estimated Subtree Cost: **0.393331**

### 6. Comparative Analysis
| Metric | Before Indexing | After Indexing | Improvement (%) |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Logical Reads | 1,232 | 447 | 63.7% |
| CPU Time (ms) | 94 | 78 | 17.0% |
| Elapsed Time (ms) | 107 | 84 | 21.5% |
| Subtree Cost | 1.49935 | 0.393331 | 73.8% |
| Operator | Clustered Index Scan | Index Seek + Agg | — |

### 7. DML Overhead
Extra index on `bookings` (2 key + 1 include, ≈ 5 MB). Same trade-off as
Query 1; the status-led index is also reused by the escalation query (RC-04)
and by the weekday/hour report (Query 4).

## Query 4 — Analytical Report: Approved Bookings by Weekday and Hour

### 1. Query Description & Business Context
Report Q2 from `outputs/16-analytical-queries-G11.sql` (RC-08): approved
bookings by weekday and hour for a semester, used for utilization planning
(when are spaces most demanded). Low frequency.

### 2. Target SQL
```sql
WITH approved AS (
    SELECT b.start_time,
           ((@@DATEFIRST + DATEPART(WEEKDAY, b.start_time) - 2) % 7) + 1
               AS weekday_number,
           DATEPART(HOUR, b.start_time) AS hour_of_day
    FROM dbo.bookings AS b
    WHERE b.status IN ('Approved', 'Checked In', 'Completed')
      AND b.start_time >= @SemStart
      AND b.start_time <  @SemEnd
)
SELECT weekday_number, hour_of_day, COUNT(*) AS approved_booking_count
FROM approved
GROUP BY weekday_number, hour_of_day
ORDER BY weekday_number, hour_of_day;
```
Benchmarked for the seed semester 2026-01-05 08:00 .. 2026-04-30 18:00.

### 3. Baseline Performance (Before Indexing)
- Plan: **Clustered Index Scan** of `bookings` (1,215 pages) + Hash Aggregate.
- Logical Reads: **1,215** · Physical Reads: 0
- CPU: **78 ms** · Elapsed: **76 ms**
- Estimated Subtree Cost: **1.37852**

### 4. Index Design & Justification
Reuses **`IX_bookings_status_time`** (status, start_time, end_time, INCLUDE
space_id) from Query 3. The status seek narrows the scan to approved-like rows;
`start_time` bounds the semester window on the key. The included `space_id` is
not needed by this aggregation but costs nothing and keeps the index shared.

### 5. Optimized Performance (After Indexing)
- Plan: **Index Seek on `IX_bookings_status_time`** + Hash Aggregate.
- Logical Reads: **430** · Physical Reads: 0
- CPU: **47 ms** · Elapsed: **52 ms**
- Estimated Subtree Cost: **0.262244**

### 6. Comparative Analysis
| Metric | Before Indexing | After Indexing | Improvement (%) |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Logical Reads | 1,215 | 430 | 64.6% |
| CPU Time (ms) | 78 | 47 | 39.7% |
| Elapsed Time (ms) | 76 | 52 | 31.6% |
| Subtree Cost | 1.37852 | 0.262244 | 81.0% |
| Operator | Clustered Index Scan | Index Seek + Agg | — |

### 7. DML Overhead
No new index — reuses `IX_bookings_status_time`. Zero additional write cost.

## Summary of Indexes Created

| Index | Table | Keys | INCLUDE | Serves |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `IX_bookings_space_time` | bookings | (space_id, start_time, end_time) | status | Q1, Q2 + concurrency range lock |
| `IX_bookings_status_time` | bookings | (status, start_time, end_time) | space_id | Q3, Q4, escalation queries |
| `IX_maintenance_records_space_time` | maintenance_records | (space_id, start_time, completion_time) | impact_level, status | Q2, booking availability |
| `IX_spaces_capacity_status` | spaces | (capacity) | current_status, space_type, space_name | Q2 room finder |

Measured index sizes on the generated dataset:
`IX_bookings_space_time` ≈ 5.0 MB · `IX_bookings_status_time` ≈ 5.0 MB ·
`IX_maintenance_records_space_time` ≈ 0.7 MB · `IX_spaces_capacity_status`
≈ 0.20 MB.

The Phase 2 indexes added after the migration (also from
`outputs/10-schema-migration-G11.sql`) — `IX_advisory_ack_booking`,
`IX_incident_reports_space_status`, `IX_consolidations_maintenance` — serve the
advisory/incident feature tables and are not part of the four benchmarked
critical paths.

## SARGability Notes
- All overlap predicates use explicit inequality form
  (`start_time < @end_time AND end_time > @start_time`) — no functions wrap the
  indexed columns, so they remain seekable.
- `DATENAME`/`DATEPART` are applied only to the projected (non-indexed) columns
  in Query 4, never in the WHERE clause, so the index is not invalidated.
- No `YEAR()`, `CAST()`, or `ISNULL()` around indexed columns anywhere in the
  four critical queries.
- All indexes are guarded with `IF NOT EXISTS` in
  `outputs/10-schema-migration-G11.sql`, so the migration is idempotent.
